cases.situation: I'm the hiring manager. Need to reject Daniel, a finalist for our senior marketing role. He was great, but the other candidate has B2B SaaS experience. I called him, now I need the follow-up email.
cases.reply: Hi Daniel, thanks again for the time you gave us, especially the launch plan you presented on Thursday, which the team is still talking about. As I said on the phone, we've offered the role to another candidate whose background is in B2B SaaS, which is where most of this role's work sits. It was a close decision. If we open the consumer marketing lead role in the spring, I'd like to contact you first, if you're open to that. Best, Farah
cases.note: Only offer the spring role if it's real; a door left open falsely is worse than none.

cases.situation: 手上有两个offer，决定去另一家了，要拒绝这家的HR张女士。面试时跟他们的李总聊得很好，不想把关系弄僵。
cases.reply: 张女士您好，非常感谢您和团队这段时间的安排，特别是和李总聊产品规划的那一轮，是我这次求职里收获最大的一次面试。经过慎重考虑，我决定接受另一家公司的offer，那个岗位和我接下来几年想做的方向更贴近。这个决定并不容易。希望以后还有机会合作，也祝团队一切顺利。
cases.note: 理由真实但简短，不说对方哪里不好，点名感谢具体的人。

cases.situation: J'ai refusé une offre dans une agence à Lyon. La DRH, Claire, m'a rappelé pour proposer 5 000 euros de plus. Ma décision n'a rien à voir avec le salaire, j'ai choisi un poste en télétravail.
cases.reply: Merci beaucoup, Claire, c'est une vraie proposition et j'y suis sensible. Ma décision ne tient pas à la rémunération mais au format du poste, donc je la maintiens. Merci encore à vous et à l'équipe pour votre accueil, j'espère qu'on se recroisera.
cases.note: Answer the counter once and honestly; saying it isn't about money closes the second round.

cases.situation: I'm in the final round for a data analyst role at Brightline Energy, panel is this Thursday. My current company just offered me the internal transfer I've wanted for a year and I've accepted. The recruiter is Nadia.
cases.reply:
Hi Nadia,
Thank you for the time you and the team have put into this, especially the conversation with Tom about the grid forecasting work, which I really enjoyed. I want to tell you early rather than late: I'm withdrawing from the process, so please do release Thursday's panel slot. I've accepted an internal move at my current company that I've been working toward for a while, and it wouldn't be fair to keep taking your team's time. I'd be glad to stay in touch.
Best,
Priya
cases.note: Withdraw before the panel, not after it: the decision by the second sentence, the true reason in one line, and freeing the slot as the practical ask.

cases.situation: 我是技术经理，组里的高级工程师小吴申请了内部的技术主管岗位，最后我们选了外部候选人。他技术很强，但带人经验还不够。明天当面谈，谈完想再给他发一条消息。
cases.reply: 小吴，谢谢你今天愿意坐下来聊，也谢谢你为这次竞聘准备的架构方案，写得非常扎实。就像当面说的，技术主管这次选了外部候选人，主要是这个岗位一上来就要带8个人，需要更多带团队的经验。这不影响我对你技术能力的判断。如果你愿意，下个季度我们让你牵头支付重构那个小组，先带两三个人，明年再有机会时你会更有底气。有什么想法，随时找我。
cases.note: 内部候选人要先当面说，再用书面补充：理由真实具体，给一个真实的下一步，而不是空泛的“以后还有机会”。

cases.situation: I'm hiring for a junior accountant. I rejected Ben after the second interview and he emailed back asking for detailed feedback, saying he thinks he was a strong fit. The one real issue: two balances in his reconciliation exercise didn't tie out.
cases.reply: Hi Ben, I understand it's disappointing, and I appreciate you asking directly. The one specific thing I'd point to is the reconciliation exercise: two of the balances didn't tie out, and that kind of accuracy is most of this role day to day. The decision is final, but it's a skill that sharpens quickly with practice, and I wish you the best with the search. Best, Farah
cases.note: A candidate who pushes back gets one more specific point you can defend, then the decision repeated kindly. Don't reopen it or promise a future role you aren't planning.

cases.situation: Got an offer from Harbor Health for a product manager role at $118k base. My current job pays $130k with bonus and I'd genuinely accept at $130k. The recruiter, Leah, wants an answer by Friday.
cases.reply: Hi Leah, thank you for the offer, and please thank Marcus for the product case discussion, which is what sold me on the team. I'd like to be transparent: the base is the one thing stopping me. At $130,000 I'd accept today, since that's what I'd be leaving behind. If there's no flexibility, I completely understand, and I'll decline with genuine thanks by Friday 2 October.
cases.note: Only name a number you would actually sign at. This is the real condition, not a bluff, so be ready to say yes if they meet it.

cases.situation: I verbally accepted an operations analyst offer from Coastline Logistics last Thursday, start date Oct 19, but haven't signed anything. Yesterday the company I've wanted for years made me an offer and I took it. I need to email the hiring manager, Greg, today and I feel awful.
cases.reply:
Hi Greg,
I'm writing to withdraw my acceptance of the operations analyst role. Yesterday I received an offer for a role I've been pursuing for over a year, and I've accepted it. I know I said yes to you on Thursday, and backing out now costs you time and a start date you'd planned around, so I wanted you to hear it today rather than later. Thank you for the time you and Renee put into the process; the warehouse walk-through was the best part of any interview I've had. I'm sorry for the disruption, and I wish you and the team the best.
Kind regards,
Maya
cases.note: Reneging on a verbal yes: tell them the day you decide, name the cost to them, and give the true reason rather than a softer invented one. Call first if you can, then send this.

cases.situation: I'm hiring a marketing coordinator. My friend Nicole referred her former colleague Jamie, who interviewed last Wednesday. Jamie was warm and really organised, but we're going with someone with more paid social experience. We'll probably hire an events assistant next spring and Jamie would suit it. I don't want this to feel awkward.
cases.reply: Hi Jamie, thank you for coming in last Wednesday, and for the event calendar you walked us through, which was one of the most organised we saw. We've decided to offer the role to another candidate whose background is heavier on paid social, which is the biggest part of the job this year. That was the deciding factor, not how you came across. We're likely to hire an events assistant next spring, and if you'd be open to it, I'd like to reach out to you directly when that opens.
cases.note: A referred candidate gets the same clear, specific no as anyone else. Tell Jamie first, and give Nicole only the outcome, never the interview details.

cases.situation: I'm hiring a UX designer. Elena did a take-home and a final interview on Aug 20, and I told her she'd hear within two weeks. It's been almost six weeks because our budget sign-off stalled, and we've now hired someone else. I need to email her today.
cases.reply:
Hi Elena,
Thank you for the time you put into the process, especially the checkout redesign, which the whole panel talked about afterwards. We've decided to offer the role to another candidate whose background is closer to our design systems work. I also told you you'd hear within two weeks, and it's been almost six. That's on me, and I'm sorry for leaving you waiting. Good luck with the search; the right team will be lucky to have you.
Best,
Marcus
cases.note: A late rejection still leads with the decision, then one plain line owning the delay. Skip the budget saga; it explains your side, not hers.

cases.situation: My close friend Aaron offered me head of operations at his 12-person startup, Pantry, after two long dinners pitching it. I'm staying at my job at Meridian for at least another year. I want to say no without it getting weird between us.
cases.reply: Aaron, thank you for the offer, and for those two dinners walking me through the plan for Pantry; I can tell how much thought has gone into it. I'm going to say no. I want to see the Meridian launch through next year, and you deserve someone who's all in from day one. I think what you're building is really good, and if you ever want a second pair of eyes on an ops problem, I'm a phone call away.
cases.note: With a friend the no still comes early, the reason is about your timing rather than their company, and you only offer help you'd actually give.

cases.situation: 我是一家贸易公司的部门经理，老板把他外甥小赵的简历转给我，让我“看看合不合适”。外贸专员这个岗位要求三年经验，他刚毕业，我面了一轮决定不录用。他对市场挺有感觉，明年春天公司可能招管培生，他很合适。要给小赵本人发邮件。
cases.reply: 小赵你好，谢谢你上周来面谈，也谢谢你准备的那份东南亚市场小调研，看得出花了心思。这次外贸专员的岗位我们决定不录用：这个岗位一上来就要独立跟海外客户，需要至少三年的外贸经验，这是岗位的硬要求。你对市场的敏感度很不错，明年春天如果公司开放管培生岗位，我会第一时间告诉你。祝求职顺利。
cases.note: 关系户也按正常标准拒，信里只讲岗位要求；跟老板那边另外单独说明，不写进给候选人的信里。

cases.situation: 领导刘总想提拔我做组长，带5个人，下个月生效。我想继续做技术，不想带人。我们关系不错，不想让他觉得我不上进。
cases.reply: 刘总，谢谢您考虑让我做组长，也谢谢上周花了一个小时跟我聊团队的规划，被您这样信任我很感激。这几天我认真想过了，决定不接这个岗位：接下来两三年我还是想专心做技术，把风控模型这块做深。这个岗位对团队很重要，您这么看重它，我更希望由真正想带人的同事来做。组长我不接，但技术上需要我多扛的，您尽管交给我。
cases.note: 拒绝上级的提拔：具体感谢、第二句就给决定，理由讲自己想走的方向而不是岗位不好，再说清楚愿意在哪方面多出力。
